standard.title: Apply grammar to predict meaning and compose complex texts
standard.description: apply knowledge of grammatical structures to predict meaning and compose texts that contain some complex structures and ideas
standard.prior_knowledge: Students apply grammatical structures including irregular verbs across tenses, expanded cohesive devices, quantity expressions and adverbial modification (AC9LS8U02). They compose in past, present and compound tenses. They have not yet worked with further tense forms for continuous or recent action, conditional or subjunctive structures, or passive constructions.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students apply grammatical structures to predict meaning and compose texts with complex structures — including further tense forms, conditional and hypothetical structures, passive voice, and expanded complex sentence types.

nodes.label: Further tense forms and conditional structures
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use further tense forms for continuous or recent action, and conditional or hypothetical structures in composition.
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least one further tense form for continuous or recent action correctly; use at least one conditional or hypothetical structure correctly.
nodes.typical_width: Apply further tense forms for continuous action or recently completed events; use conditional structures for real and hypothetical scenarios; use hypothetical or subjunctive forms where appropriate in the target language; apply perfect aspect forms for completed action.
wider: Write a text using at least three different tense and aspect forms — each with a margin note explaining the temporal or aspectual purpose
Produce a conditional scenario — describing what would happen if something were different — using the correct conditional structure throughout
nodes.hinge_reason: Further tense and conditional structures are the grammatical tools for expressing continuous, recently completed and hypothetical meaning — all required for sophisticated narrative, analytical and persuasive composition at this band.

response_modes.reason: Complex tense and conditional accuracy requires repeated production practice in varied composition contexts. Understanding the distinction intellectually does not prevent production errors under pressure.

success_criteria: Uses at least one further tense form correctly in composition
Uses at least one conditional or hypothetical structure correctly

nodes.label: Passive voice and complex sentence types
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use passive voice constructions and complex sentence types — including relative clauses and expanded subordinate structures.
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least one passive construction correctly; use at least one relative clause or complex subordinate structure correctly.
nodes.typical_width: Use passive constructions for impersonal and formal purposes; form relative clauses to embed information; use complex subordinate structures to express causation, condition and time relationships; combine structures to produce genuinely complex sentences.
wider: Produce a paragraph using at least three different complex sentence types — identify each type and explain the meaning relationship it creates
Revise a simple text by embedding information using relative clauses — compare before and after, explaining how each addition changes information density

response_modes.reason: Passive and complex sentence structures develop through encountering and producing them across varied text types and purposes. Each new text context draws on different complex structures.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Passive voice and relative clauses are what move target language composition into genuinely complex territory — producing texts with information density and structural sophistication comparable to authentic native speaker writing.
success_criteria: Uses at least one passive construction correctly in a composition context
Uses at least one relative clause or complex subordinate structure correctly

nodes.label: Using grammar to predict meaning in complex texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use grammatical knowledge to predict and confirm meaning in complex target language texts — including texts with unfamiliar vocabulary.
nodes.minimum_width: Use grammatical knowledge to predict the meaning of at least two unfamiliar words or structures in a complex text — explain the reasoning used.
nodes.typical_width: Apply grammatical knowledge to interpret complex texts; use sentence structure and word class knowledge to predict unfamiliar meaning; identify how grammatical features signal relationships between ideas in complex texts; use grammar as a comprehension tool in authentic reading and listening.
wider: Work through a complex authentic target language text — for every unfamiliar word, use grammar and context to predict meaning before checking a reference
Explain the grammatical reasoning behind at least three predictions made in a complex text — demonstrating explicit metalinguistic awareness of the prediction process

response_modes.reason: Using grammar as a comprehension tool requires students to articulate the reasoning — not only guess intuitively. Structured prediction tasks with explicit reasoning make the metalinguistic process visible.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Using grammar as a comprehension tool transforms grammatical knowledge from a production resource into a general-purpose meaning-making tool — enabling genuine independent engagement with complex authentic texts.
success_criteria: Uses grammatical knowledge to predict the meaning of at least two unfamiliar items in a complex text
Explains the grammatical reasoning used for at least one prediction
